Title: Yinson Production eyes expansion after US$1.46bil refinancing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Yinson Production's US$1.458 billion (RM5.9 billion) Agogo floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) project bond refinancing has freed up financing capacity for new projects as the company eyes expansion across Southeast Asia, West Africa and Latin America.
Chief financial officer Markus Wenker said the refinancing allowed the company to repay about US$1.4 billion in existing loans, freeing up lending capacity among its financiers to support future projects.
He said Yinson Production had diversified its funding sources over the past four years, reducing its reliance on bank loans to a financing mix of about 75 per cent bank funding and 25 per cent institutional investment.
"The US$1.458 billion Agogo FPSO project bond was our third in three years, the largest FPSO project bond ever issued and the first outside Brazil.
"Project bonds have become a key instrument in our financing playbook, and I expect us to continue using them where they offer the best financing solution," he said in a media briefing on Thursday.
Wenker said the company had access to several billion US dollars in debt financing to support its growth plans.
"There still seems to be a perception that capital for large offshore projects is not available. Our financing track record over the last few years demonstrates quite the opposite," he said.
He added that investors remained willing to provide long-term funding for projects with sound risk profiles and contracted cash flows.
Chief executive officer Flemming Guiducci Grønnegaard said the company continued to see a healthy pipeline of FPSO opportunities, particularly in the mid-sized segment, across its key markets.
"The fundamentals of the offshore energy market remain strong, and we continue to see a healthy pipeline of FPSO opportunities.
"We have built the organisation and capabilities to manage four or five major projects concurrently, but growth for us is not about chasing volume. We will remain selective and pursue the projects where we believe we can create the greatest long-term value," he said.
Grønnegaard said the company was exploring opportunities in Suriname and Guyana, while Namibia could offer further potential as its oil and gas investment policies develop.
He also reaffirmed Yinson Production's preference for the lease-and-operate model, which allows the company to maintain long-term client relationships rather than simply build and hand over assets.
Beyond FPSOs, the company is developing capabilities in floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG), having begun recruiting key personnel earlier this year.
Grønnegaard described FLNG as a natural extension of its business, drawing on the company's experience in developing, financing, owning and operating offshore infrastructure.
Wenker said traditional bank financing had become more challenging due to regulatory constraints, while several Western export credit agencies had withdrawn from financing new FPSO projects over environmental, social and governance concerns.
Nevertheless, he said lenders and investors remained willing to finance high-quality offshore infrastructure backed by credible sponsors and long-term contracted cash flows.

Title: Mega Fortris sheds RM1.75bil in seven-day rout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mega Fortris Bhd's spectacular stock market rally has unravelled in just seven trading days, wiping out about RM1.75 billion in market value as its shares plunged 60 per cent from their record high.
The security seals manufacturer, whose shares had nearly quadrupled in value this year, suffered another bruising session on Friday, triggering a third consecutive intraday short-selling (IDSS) suspension.
At 10.08am, Mega Fortris was trading at RM1.38, down 45 sen, or 24.59 per cent, from Thursday's closing price of RM1.83.
The latest plunge brought its market capitalisation down to about RM1.17 billion from RM2.92 billion on Oct 28, when the stock closed at an all-time high of RM3.45.
It marks a dramatic reversal for a counter that had been among the market's standout performers this year.
Mega Fortris began 2026 at 87.5 sen before embarking on a remarkable climb that saw its shares surge 294.29 per cent to RM3.45 on Oct 27 and 28.
But the rally came to an abrupt halt on Oct 29, when the stock tumbled 71 sen, or 20.58 per cent, to RM2.74.
The selling intensified the following day, dragging the shares down to RM2.22 at last Friday's close.
The stock staged a brief comeback on Monday, jumping 29.73 per cent to RM2.88, but the recovery proved short-lived.
By Wednesday, Mega Fortris had slipped to RM2.54 before suffering another steep fall to RM1.83 on Thursday.
Despite the collapse, its shares remain 50.5 sen, or 57.71 per cent, above their starting price for the year.
IDSS of Mega Fortris shares has been suspended for the remainder of today after the stock breached the prescribed price limit.
It will resume on Tuesday (Nov 10) at 8.30am as the market will be closed on Monday for the Deepavali public holiday.
The sharp decline follows a turbulent week for Mega Fortris and two other Bursa Malaysia-listed companies, GIIB Holdings Bhd and Ni Hsin Group Bhd, which have also suffered heavy selling pressure.
Ng, who chairs Mega Fortris and controls about 67 per cent of the company, holds a combined 15.82 per cent stake in GIIB, according to Bursa Malaysia data.
The Edge reported that Ng also held a 2.22 per cent stake in Ni Hsin, but checks on Bursa Malaysia's shareholder data showed that he was no longer among the company's 10 largest shareholders.
GIIB closed Thursday at 32 sen, down 9.5 sen, or 22.89 per cent, after rebounding to 50 sen on Monday.
Ni Hsin, meanwhile, fell 6.5 sen, or 25 per cent, to 19.5 sen on Thursday, having recovered to 34 sen earlier in the week.
The sharp swings prompted Bursa Malaysia to issue unusual market activity queries to all three companies.
In its response, Mega Fortris disclosed that Ng and substantial shareholder Mega Fortris Global Pte Ltd had obtained a court order seeking documents relating to transactions involving 17.74 million Mega Fortris shares between March 25 and 31 this year.
The company said it could not determine whether the court proceedings were linked to the recent share price decline.

Title: F&N Q4 net profit rises 18.2pct on lower tax expenses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd's (F&N) net profit rose 18.2 per cent to RM135.05 million in the fourth quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM114.29 million a year earlier, mainly due to lower tax expenses.
Revenue, however, declined 3.1 per cent to RM1.19 billion from RM1.23 billion, reflecting changes in product mix and promotional activities.
The group's quarterly operating profit remained largely unchanged at RM173.7 million, compared with RM173.8 million a year earlier, it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
F&N said its performance was partly affected by higher operating costs at F&N AgriValley, weaker results from its food and beverage operations in Indochina and unfavourable foreign exchange movements.
For the full financial year, net profit fell 14 per cent to RM437.09 million from RM508.47 million in FY2025, while revenue declined 5.3 per cent to RM4.92 billion from RM5.20 billion.
The group attributed the weaker full-year performance to higher costs associated with its new investments, continued sales disruptions in Cambodia and unfavourable currency movements.
Its Malaysian operations recorded revenue growth of 3.3 per cent to RM3.06 billion from RM2.96 billion, supported by stronger domestic sales of beverages, water and dairy products.
Growth was also driven by wider distribution and stronger execution across modern trade, traditional trade and hotel, restaurant and café channels.
Export volumes increased on stronger market penetration across Africa, Asean and other markets, although the weaker US dollar against the ringgit weighed on export revenue.
Meanwhile, revenue from its Indochina operations fell 16.6 per cent to RM1.86 billion from RM2.23 billion, affected by continued border disruptions affecting sales to Cambodia, subdued economic conditions and weaker tourism activity in Thailand.
F&N group chief executive officer Tarang Gupta said Malaysia and Thailand remained the group's two established business pillars, supported by strong brands, consumer loyalty and disciplined commercial execution.
"The volume growth achieved across our core businesses, despite challenging market conditions, reinforces our confidence in their underlying strength," he said.
Tarang said the group was also focused on stabilising and expanding its two newer businesses, F&N AgriValley and its manufacturing operations in Cambodia.
At F&N AgriValley, milk yields reached 30 litres per cow per day, three times the Malaysian industry average of 10 litres, despite challenging weather conditions.
He said the performance demonstrated the potential of the group's integrated dairy operations to contribute towards Malaysia's fresh milk self-sufficiency.
F&N also continued to expand its market presence and distribution network under its Reach Competitively strategy, including through a digitally enabled van sales model targeting underserved on-premise channels.
The group introduced new 100PLUS ZERO flavours, convenient Magnolia milk products for children and an expanded range of NutriWell plant-based beverages to meet changing consumer preferences.
Looking ahead, F&N said it would focus on strengthening commercial execution and improving operational efficiency to support growth.
At F&N AgriValley, its immediate priority is to improve productivity and operating efficiency as its integrated dairy operations expand.
In Cambodia, following the start of local manufacturing operations in October, the group plans to gradually increase production, strengthen distribution and expand its market presence.
F&N said the new manufacturing facility would improve its ability to serve the Cambodian market and support the growth of its Gold Coin business.
The group proposed a final dividend of 30 sen per share, down from 35 sen a year earlier, bringing its total dividend for FY2026 to 60 sen per share.

Title: Rosmah's bid to adduce new evidence: Further case management on Jan 14
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here has fixed Jan 14 next year for further case management of Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor's application to adduce additional evidence in her RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project corruption case.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin fixed the date today after being informed that the prosecution's appeal at the Federal Court against the Court of Appeal's decision allowing Rosmah to introduce the additional evidence was still pending.
Rosmah's lawyer, Datuk Akberdin Abdul Kader, told the court that the Court of Appeal's grounds of judgment had yet to be made available for the Federal Court to complete the appeal records.
Akberdin said the appellate court had fixed Nov 25 for case management to update the status of the matter, while another mention was scheduled for Dec 3.
"We are still not ready," he said, requesting more time to allow the Federal Court proceedings to be dealt with first.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohamad Mustaffa P. Kunyalam also confirmed that the prosecution was still waiting for the grounds of judgment.
On Sept 1, the Court of Appeal allowed
Rosmah's application
to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence in the solar hybrid project corruption case.
A three-member bench chaired by Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli ordered that the additional evidence from prosecution witness Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah be recorded before a High Court judge.
The additional evidence involved a police report and a statutory declaration by Rayyan, who alleged that he had been pressured by the prosecution during the trial.
However, the prosecution filed an appeal at the Federal Court on Sept 4 to challenge the decision.
On Sept 17, the Court of Appeal granted the prosecution's application to stay the order allowing the additional evidence to be recorded pending the disposal of its appeal at the Federal Court.
On Sept 1, 2022, Rosmah was convicted of three corruption charges involving the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project for 369 rural schools in Sarawak.
She was found guilty of soliciting RM187.5 million and receiving RM6.5 million in bribes from former Jepak Holdings Sdn Bhd managing director Saidi Abang Samsudin through her former aide, Datuk Rizal Mansor.
The gratification was an inducement to help Jepak Holdings secure the project from the Education Ministry.
Rosmah was sentenced to 10 years in jail on each charge, to run concurrently, and fined RM970 million.
She was granted a stay of execution pending the disposal of her appeal against the conviction and sentence.

Title: Fahmi leads Malaysia's bid for re-election to ITU Council
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil is leading Malaysia's delegation to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26) in Doha, Qatar, from Nov 6 to 11.
The visit comes as Malaysia seeks re-election to the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.
Malaysia's participation in the quadrennial conference, the ITU's highest decision-making platform, aims to ensure the country's interests remain represented in shaping global telecommunications and information and communications technology (ICT) policies.
The conference will chart the ITU's policies and strategic plans for 2027 to 2030, while electing its top leadership, members of the Radio Regulations Board, and 48 member states to the ITU Council.
The cabinet approved Malaysia's re-election bid through the Communications Ministry on June 5, 2025, and endorsed Fahmi as head of the delegation on Sept 2 this year.
Malaysia aims to reinforce its role in shaping international telecommunications policies while engaging fellow member states to muster support for its candidacy.
Securing a seat on the ITU Council would allow Malaysia to participate directly in decisions steering global telecommunications and ICT development, including digital infrastructure, technology standards, cybersecurity, and initiatives to bridge the digital divide.
The 48-member council acts as the union's governing body between plenipotentiary conferences, overseeing policy implementation, strategic planning, finances, and work programmes.
Re-election would also enable Malaysia to contribute to international regulations and standards, especially technological compatibility and interoperability, while fostering a more inclusive and sustainable digital ecosystem.
Membership would further elevate Malaysia's digital diplomacy, international footprint, and cooperation with other member states, particularly across the Asia-Pacific region.
Malaysia joined the ITU on Feb 3, 1958, and served four consecutive terms on the council from 1998 to 2014 before winning a seat for the 2023-2026 term at PP-22 in Bucharest, Romania.
Fahmi is scheduled to attend the heads of delegation meeting, the opening ceremony, and the plenary session on Nov 9, where he will deliver Malaysia's national policy statement.
He will also take part in a high-level thematic discussion on strategic telecommunications and ICT development issues.
Malaysia will host a luncheon at the conference venue to deepen diplomatic ties with member states and showcase its achievements during its 2023-2026 council tenure.
Ahead of the conference, Fahmi is scheduled to meet the Malaysian diaspora in Doha, including representatives of the Malaysian Association in Qatar, the Malaysian Business Executive Council-Qatar, community groups, and students.
He is also expected to attend Sukan Malaysia Qatar, organised by the Malaysian Association of Qatar alongside the Malaysian diplomatic mission in Doha. — BERNAMA

Title: Sarawak polls set for Dec 12
Article:
KUCHING: The 13th Sarawak state election will be held on Dec 12.
Election Commission chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said Nov 28 had been set for nomination day, while early voting would be held on Dec 8. The election writ was issued today.
He said the EC had received official notification of the dissolution from the Sarawak state assembly speaker before deciding to hold the election for all 82 seats.
"Applications for all categories of postal voting, both within and outside the country, have been open since Oct 26," he said at a press conference.
The EC has appointed 82 returning officers, assisted by 305 assistant returning officers throughout Sarawak.
The EC has also set up 82 election campaign enforcement teams to monitor campaign activities throughout the official campaign period. The teams comprise representatives from the police, local authorities and contesting candidates.
Ramlan said the electoral roll to be used was the latest register up to the September 2026 Supplementary Electoral Roll, updated as of Oct 25.
There are 2,058,781 registered voters in Sarawak.
Of the total, 13,575 are military personnel and 10,833 policemen, along with their spouses.

Title: Malicious WhatsApp ZIP files can steal passwords, banking details, expert warns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Suspicious ZIP files circulated through messaging platforms such as WhatsApp could expose users to malware that steals passwords, banking credentials and personal information, said an expert.
Deputy Dean (Academic and Technology) of the Malaysian Institute of Information Technology, Universiti Kuala Lumpur (UniKL MIIT), Dr Shafiza Mohd Shariff, said the malware could collect information stored on users' devices, including login credentials, and monitor their banking activities.
She said the malicious software could capture users' keystrokes, collect passwords and other login credentials, access information stored on their devices and monitor their activities, particularly those involving financial applications.
"They can also monitor your device usage, especially if it is financial, such as banking and so on. They will be able to capture your credentials," she said.
Shafiza said attackers could also divert Transaction Authorisation Code (TAC) numbers to their phones if users accessed applications that still relied on the verification method, potentially allowing them to receive the codes without users' knowledge.
She said many mobile phone users did not have antivirus software installed, leaving their devices more vulnerable to malicious attachments circulated through platforms such as WhatsApp and Telegram.
At the same time, she advised users to contact the sender to verify suspicious files and avoid downloading or opening attachments from unknown sources.
"You can call the person who sent (the files to) you and check with them. If it comes from somebody you do not know, do not download it or open it," she said.
She also recommended installing antivirus software on mobile devices and keeping it running in the background at all times to detect and quarantine malicious files.
On Oct 29, the Malaysia Computer Emergency Response Team (MyCERT) issued an advisory on an active campaign in Malaysia involving malicious files disguised as financial and payment documents and distributed through WhatsApp.
According to MyCERT, the files were disguised as invoices, statements of account, electronic statements and compiled payment documents, with recipients instructed to open or extract the ZIP attachments on a computer.
MyCERT said its analysis found that running the programmes embedded in the ZIP archives could install remote-control malware on Windows computers, potentially giving attackers control over affected devices.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in a Nov 4 advisory, warned of increased risks involving suspicious ZIP files, attachments and links circulated through WhatsApp.
MCMC said scammers might impersonate known individuals or trusted parties to persuade recipients to open suspicious files or follow links, potentially resulting in malware infections, personal information leaks, unauthorised access to devices or WhatsApp accounts, and account takeovers. —BERNAMA

Title: [UPDATED] Rosmah unaware of plans to pay Najib's RM50mil fine
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor said she was unaware of any arrangements to pay the RM50 million fine imposed on her husband, Datuk Seri Najib Razak, to enable him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Rosmah said she had not been informed of any developments concerning the payment today.
"I do not know. You all know better.
"The family does not know and I am not being told about it," she said when approached by reporters at the Kuala Lumpur courts complex today.
She was met after attending the hearing of her application to adduce new evidence in her solar hybrid project corruption case.
When shown a news report by a Malay daily claiming that two people believed to be Najib's representatives had been spotted at the court's payment counter this morning, Rosmah appeared puzzled and asked who the individuals were.
"They (Malay daily) always know better and then after that they retract," she said with a giggle.
Rosmah also said she was unaware of the progress of Umno's crowdfunding campaign to raise RM50 million to help Najib settle the fine.
"I am not involved in it. You can ask Asyraf Wajdi," she said, referring to Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
Earlier today, Utusan Malaysia reported that two people believed to be representing Najib were seen leaving the payment counter at the Kuala Lumpur courts complex.
The report said they were believed to have visited the counter to obtain information on the procedures for paying the fine.
On Wednesday, Asyraf Wajdi denied reports that Najib was preparing to settle the fine, saying the
crowdfunding campaign
had yet to raise the required amount.
He also declined to disclose the amount collected through the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund, which was launched on Sept 18.
Najib's lawyer, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, had also dismissed speculation over the payment, saying he had not received any instructions from his client to settle the fine.
On Sunday, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar confirmed that Najib had yet to
pay the fine
and that no specific deadline had been set for the payment.
On Sept 18, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his jail term under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and other conditions.
Najib, 73, has been serving
his sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction for misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd.
He was originally sentenced to 12 years in jail and fined RM210 million.
In January 2024, the Federal Territories
Pardons Board reduced his jail term
to six years and the fine to RM50 million.8

Title: Hindus to celebrate Deepavali on Sunday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hindus across the country will celebrate Deepavali on Nov 8 with traditional prayers, religious rituals and family gatherings marking the Festival of Lights.
Deepavali, also known as Diwali, is one of the most significant celebrations in the Hindu calendar, symbolising the triumph of good over evil, light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance.
The lighting of oil lamps, or
agal vilakku
, is among the festival's key traditions, representing the removal of darkness and the welcoming of hope, positivity and prosperity.
Malaysia Hindhudharma Maamandram President Rishi Kumar Vadivelu said Deepavali also serves as a reminder for devotees to overcome negative traits such as arrogance, jealousy and ego.
He said the word Deepavali originated from the Tamil words
Deepam
, meaning oil lamp, and
Avali
, meaning a row or arrangement of lamps.
Preparations traditionally begin on the eve of Deepavali on Nov 7 when families perform prayers to honour their clan deity (
Kula Deivam
) and seek blessings.
"On Deepavali morning, families observe the traditional
Ganga Snanam
ritual, which involves applying sesame oil to the head before bathing, a practice believed to bring spiritual blessings," he told Bernama.
After the ritual, family members wear new clothes, seek blessings from parents and elders, offer prayers and visit temples before returning home to enjoy traditional meals and sweets with family and friends.
Homes are also decorated with oil lamps and colourful
kolam
designs, while families prepare various festive delicacies to share with visitors.
Meanwhile, Malaysia Hindu Sangam National President Thanga Ganesan said Deepavali was an important occasion to strengthen family ties and preserve cultural and religious traditions for future generations.
He encouraged Malaysians to share the joy of the celebration with friends from other communities through open house invitations and gatherings.
"In our multiracial Malaysia, let us share the joy of Deepavali with our Malay, Chinese and other friends from diverse communities. Through mutual respect, understanding and unity, we can further strengthen the harmony that makes our nation unique," he said.
Meanwhile, MIC vice-president and former deputy minister in the Prime Minister's Department Datuk T. Murugiah in his Deepavali greetings called on the Indian community to use the festival as an opportunity to strengthen family relationships, promote unity and extend assistance to the less fortunate.
He also urged the government to give greater attention to the welfare, education, employment opportunities and economic development of the Indian community, particularly families in the B40 income group.
Murugiah said the spirit of Deepavali should go beyond festive celebrations and inspire Malaysians to practise kindness, compassion and mutual respect while strengthening harmony in the country's multiracial society.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 4 arrested over Teluk Intan murder
Article:
TELUK INTAN: Police have arrested four people, including two foreign men, to assist investigations into the murder of a man in Taman Banjar Jaya on Tuesday.
Hilir Perak district police chief Assistant Commissioner Chua Kok Lian said the latest arrest involved a man detained yesterday. An application to remand him was expected to be made this morning.
He said three other suspects, comprising a woman and two foreign men, were arrested in the early hours of Nov 4 and remanded until Nov 11.
Chua said the latest suspect was aged between 30 and 40.
In the incident at 3.53pm on Nov 3, a man was believed to have been attacked with a sharp weapon at a shop in Teluk Intan.
The victim, who suffered serious injuries, was taken to Teluk Intan Hospital but was pronounced dead.
Initial investigations found that the victim was attacked by three men armed with parang. The motive remains under investigation.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.

Title: Will there be real change post-US midterms?
Article:
LETTER:
The United States midterms election produced a genuine political earthquake, yet the structural forces that produced the current brand of divisive politics remain largely intact.
Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress but the uncomfortable part for anyone expecting a clean break is that the Democrats won without a fixed, unified programme.
International reactions suggest a cautious, conditional yes — but with low expectations of transformation post-US midterms election.
European leaders welcomed the result primarily as a relief: a signal that American voters had rejected the war and the climate denialism and the contempt for alliances.
The European Parliament's vice-president voiced the prevailing mood: optimism "not because everything will suddenly get better, but because this could be good for support for Ukraine, the green transition, and relations with the rest of the world".
The qualifier is doing the heavy lifting.
Iran's supreme leader was more cynical, saying anyone expecting US policy to shift based on party changes is "sorely mistaken". Russia shrugged.
The world, in other words, has learned to distinguish between American rhetoric and American continuity. Allies will take the tonal shift. They are not betting on a structural one.
America changed its government. It did not change its politics. The midterms were a rejection of one man's governance, not a ratification of an alternative vision.
The new leadership inherits the same polarised electorate, the same money-soaked machinery, and the same structural veto points that make dramatic change nearly impossible in a two-year window.
The world can accept this version of something different — a less belligerent Washington, a Congress that takes oversight seriously — because the bar is low and the relief is genuine.
But if the expectation is a fundamental reset, the answer is the one your friend the dinosaur-hunter might not want to hear: the species survives. It just changes its skin.
There's a seductive simplicity to the story: voters spoke, the old guard fell, and renewal is on the march. It's a story both sides of the Atlantic are telling themselves.
But before we applaud the extinction of the "dinosaurs," it's worth asking who exactly gets to define a dinosaur — and whether replacing the old faces has ever, by itself, produced the change people are hungry for.
The frustration is real and legitimate. But here's where the argument needs to get honest.
History is littered with "new guards" that learned the old tricks faster than anyone expected.
What would a genuinely different politics look like? It would mean being precise about problems rather than dramatic about enemies.
It would mean politicians who can articulate what they're for rather than only what they're against.
It would mean voters willing to reward competence and punish unseriousness, not just reward the loudest voice.
And it would mean accepting that pluralism is not a disease to be cured by one decisive victory.
PROFESSOR DATUK DR AHMAD IBRAHIM
Tan Sri Omar Centre for STI Policy
UCSI University

Title: Rubio denies plans to leave post for White House bid
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio dismissed reports on Thursday that he was planning to leave the Trump administration as he weighs his next moves after Republicans' losses in the midterm elections, according to The New York Times.
It has "always been my plan" to work for President Donald Trump until the end of his term, Rubio told The Times in an interview.
Rubio, who also serves as Trump's national security adviser, is widely considered a potential successor to Trump in the 2028 presidential race.
Just days before Tuesday's midterm elections, he made an unusual appearance alongside the US leader on the campaign trail, briefly stepping up to the podium to address a cheering crowd at a rally.
Rubio declined to answer questions about his political future on Thursday, however, saying: "I literally will not talk about 2028 anymore."
On reports that he was considering leaving the Trump administration, he told The New York Times: "I don't know where these things come from, to be honest with you."
Earlier on Thursday, Bloomberg News reported that Rubio was weighing whether to leave the administration.
The report added that Rubio had spoken to White House officials about stepping down and was asked to stay.
But the State Department has hit back sharply against reports that Rubio might leave.
Dylan Johnson, Assistant Secretary of State for global public affairs, called the Bloomberg article "totally made up".
He also called a report by news outlet The Independent, which said Rubio was planning to launch a bid for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, "completely baseless fake news".
Rubio has previously said that he would support Vice President JD Vance if he ran for president.
Vance is also widely considered a possible 2028 candidate.

Title: Higher CPO prices to cushion SD Guthrie's weaker output
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Higher crude palm oil (CPO) prices in financial year 2027 (FY27) are likely to cushion the impact of weaker production at SD Guthrie Bhd following dry weather that affected its yields, said CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
In a note, the firm said SD Guthrie sees CPO prices potentially reaching RM5,000 per tonne in 2027 as supply conditions tighten. However, high Malaysian inventories continue to weigh on near-term prices.
"Higher CPO prices could cushion weaker production, although the net earnings benefit will depend on the extent of yield losses, unit-cost increases and realised selling prices," it said.
SD Guthrie's Indonesian estates experienced around four months of severe drought, which could reduce fresh fruit bunch (FFB) yields and output with a six- to 18-month lag, extending into early FY28.
"Management expects FY27 production growth in Malaysia and Papua New Guinea but lower output in Indonesia, without providing firm guidance.
"Indonesia's agrarian reform also adds uncertainty over compliance with the 20 per cent plasma obligation. The group is exploring alternative community-support programmes where additional land is unavailable, but implementation details and compliance costs remain unclear," said CIMB Securities.
The firm also said higher wages and fertiliser costs are expected to add about one per cent and 1.4 per cent, respectively, to production costs in FY27.
SD Guthrie's core net profit of RM821 million in the third quarter brought its nine-month core earnings to RM2.3 billion, representing 75 per cent of CIMB Securities' FY26 forecast of RM3.08 billion and broadly meeting expectations.
The firm maintained its earnings forecasts for SD Guthrie, implying core earnings of RM774 million in the fourth quarter.
It said provision write-backs were not expected to recur, while lower CPO prices and production were likely to weigh on plantation earnings.
"These headwinds should be partly offset by RM290 million in net profit from industrial land sales and RM68 million in land compensation."
CIMB Securities maintained its "Buy" call on the stock with a target price of RM6.52.

Title: Foreign drivers rack up 133,081 summonses in eight months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 133,081 summonses were issued to foreign drivers between January and August this year, with 21,232 cases involving driving without a Competent Driving Licence (CDL).
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said during the same period, 1,933 cases of driving without a Goods Driving Licence (GDL) were also recorded.
He said 85 cases of driving without a Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licence were logged during the first eight months of the year.
"Other offences include expired Motor Vehicle Licences (LKM), lack of insurance coverage, absence of an entry permit or International Circulation Permit (ICP), and overloading.
"To ensure repeat offences are curbed, continuous enforcement and integrated operations are being carried out, including document checks on drivers and vehicles," he said in a written reply published on the parliament website today.
He was responding to a question from Dr Siti Mastura Muhammad (PN-Kepala Batas) on the total number of cases recorded and the follow-up actions taken to prevent repeat offences.
Loke said action was also taken against vehicles violating regulations through collaboration with the Immigration Department and the police, particularly for cases involving immigration status or other offences.
"The ministry emphasises the responsibility of vehicle owners and employers to ensure only individuals with valid driving licences are permitted to drive on the road.
"Accordingly, the Road Transport Department (RTD) will continue to intensify targeted operations in high-risk locations and sectors.
"This is to improve legal compliance among drivers, vehicle owners, and employers, including those involving foreigners," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Google sued over suicide-related AI chats on school computer
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google, claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer.
Filed on Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant's low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world.
The teenager, identified by the name Emma, was unable to access Google's Gemini app or OpenAI's ChatGPT because they were blocked by her school.
She was nonetheless still able to use Google's search engine, which contains AI-powered tools.
Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week would be disabled by default for students.
"Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they're interacting with AI," Andrew Liddell, one of the family's lawyers, told AFP on Thursday.
The complaint alleges that Emma had been a "happy 13-year-old girl" in North Carolina who received good grades, played music and participated in the Girl Scouts.
Despite having "no history" of mental illness, within months of using Google's AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a "quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis", according to the complaint.
On March 17, the school's monitoring software flagged a document titled "Funeral", and the school notified her parents.
Her mother then saw Emma writing a farewell letter in real time after logging into her daughter's account, and her father intervened.
"We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously," Google spokesman Jose Castaneda told AFP.
Google argues that AI mode includes safeguards against self-harm and attempts to bypass them.
But Emma "was able to keep going back over and over and over again", Liddell said. "Whatever safeguards they think they put in place were obviously insufficient."
Developers of fast-evolving AI technology are facing a litany of similar lawsuits in the US.
OpenAI faces several wrongful death suits, including one filed by the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, a teenager who allegedly died by suicide using methods advised by ChatGPT.
Google and the startup Character.AI agreed in January to settle several lawsuits filed by families of teenagers out of court.
On Wednesday, Google, TikTok and Meta each separately sued California to block a law that prohibits social media companies from providing addictive features to users under 16.
Governor Gavin Newsom signed the law in September, and it takes effect on Jan 1, 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Motorcyclist drowns after skidding into river in Mersing
Article:
MERSING: A motorcyclist drowned after skidding into Sungai Jemaluang in Jalan Sekakap last night.
Mersing district police chief Superintendent Abdul Razak Abdullah Sani said police received information about the accident at 11.15pm.
The victim's body was found at 7.50am today after a search operation.
Senior Operations Commander Mohd Alias Hussin said the fire and rescue department received an emergency call about the incident at 11.26pm.
Firefighters from the Mersing Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene near a shrimp pond in Jalan Sekakap, Seri Pantai.

Alias said the body was found about 100m from the last location where the victim was seen before being handed over to the police.

Title: Malaysia at risk of becoming transit hub for international drug syndicates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia faces the threat of being exploited as a transit hub for international drug smuggling and trafficking syndicates.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the country's strategic geographical location and extensive air, land, and maritime transport networks could potentially be leveraged by organised crime syndicates to bring in drugs before distributing them to local markets or forwarding them to other destination countries.
He said the matter was uncovered through intelligence and enforcement operations by the police.
"The police, through the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID), are intensifying intelligence gathering and enforcement operations against the entire syndicate network.
"This includes suppliers, coordinators, financiers, and distributors, alongside strengthening cooperation with international enforcement agencies and tightening controls at airports, ports, and land borders to curb smuggling activities," he said in a written reply published on the Dewan Rakyat portal today.
He was responding to a question from Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka) on whether Malaysia is currently serving as a transit point for international drug production and trafficking syndicates.
Saifuddin said that, following several security incidents at the country's entry points, the cabinet approved a Joint Memorandum between the Home Ministry and the Transport Ministry on Aug 19.
He said the memorandum covers the proposed implementation of an action plan on Security Improvement and Mitigation to Strengthen Security Controls and Screening in phases at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and other international entry points.
"This action plan encompasses 17 substantive recommendations framed around three main security pillars: Aviation Security, National and Border Security, and Physical and Protection Security.
"Its implementation is divided into phases comprising short-term (zero to six months), medium-term (six to 24 months), and long-term (exceeding 24 months)," he said.

Title: Speaker tells ministers, deputy ministers to arrive early for Dewan Rakyat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul reminded members of the administration to arrive early to answer questions and avoid unseemly absences during proceedings.
Johari made the reprimand after an incident during the morning sitting yesterday when several questions went unanswered because the relevant parties were absent.

"I advise members of the administration to arrive early in the chamber, even if your question number is later in the order," he said before starting the winding-up session on the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 committee-stage debate and Development Expenditure Estimates for the Rural and Regional Development Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
Earlier, several opposition MPs questioned the absence of Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad and his deputy, Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib, during the oral question-and-answer session.
Their absence was noted after Deputy Speaker Alice Lau called on Zahir Hassan (PH-Wangsa Maju) to ask the third question, directed to the Health Ministry, as listed in the Order Paper.
During the session, the second question scheduled for the Transport Ministry was skipped because the Kepala Batas MP, who was supposed to table it, was not present in the chamber, leading the sitting to move on to the next question.

Title: CAP warns of threat from invasive species in waterways
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A consumer watchdog has warned the release of non-native species into local waterways threatens biodiversity, ecosystems and the livelihoods of fishing communities.
Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) president Mohideen Abdul Kader said urgent action was needed to stop the introduction of foreign fish, plants, snails and mussels into Malaysia's rivers, lakes, dams and coastal waters.
"These invasive species outcompete native life, disrupt delicate ecosystems, and jeopardise the livelihoods of riverine and fishing communities," he said in a statement.
The Fisheries Department has removed more than 4.4 tonnes of non-native fish from Malaysian waters since 2022 through
17 operations
targeting invasive species.
Its director-general Datuk Adnan Hussain said the operations targeted aggressive, fast-breeding foreign species that threaten local biodiversity by competing for food and habitat.
Mohideen also highlighted the spread of water hyacinth, known locally as keladi bunting or bunga kiambang.
Native to South America's Amazon Basin, the fast-growing plant can choke waterways and degrade water quality when released into the environment.
The invasive Chinese pond mussel (Sinanodonta woodiana) has colonised at least 10 river basins in Peninsular Malaysia and six across Sabah and Sarawak, according to the Handbook and National Red-List of the Freshwater Mussels of Malaysia.
Its spread has been linked to intentional introductions for food and trade, as well as live freshwater fish shipments inadvertently carrying its parasitic larvae.
In rural areas, giant African land snails and golden apple snails (Pomacea canaliculata and Pomacea maculata) damage paddy fields after escaping from food and aquarium setups.
Mohideen said non-native farmed fish routinely escaped into natural habitats during flash floods, storms or because of poor pond containment.
He urged the Fisheries Department and Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department to tighten controls on the import, commercial breeding, sale and transit of non-native aquatic species.
He also called on fish farms to strengthen biosecurity and ornamental pet vendors to educate buyers against releasing unwanted species into waterways.
"Hobbyists must stop treating drains, canals and rivers as dumping grounds for overgrown pets or unwanted plants. Those unable to keep exotic species should surrender them to relevant wildlife or fisheries authorities instead," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MRT Corp awards RM2.69bil contract for Penang LRT sea-crossing link
Article:
PENANG: Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) has awarded the RM2.69 billion Civil Main Contract 2 (CMC2) package for the Mutiara Line light rail transit (LRT) project to a joint venture comprising China Communications Construction Company, TRC Construction and Ufuk Semarak.
The joint venture, known as CCCC-TRC-UFUK JV, will undertake the design and construction of an estimated 5.5km alignment linking Macallum on Penang island to Penang Sentral on the mainland.
A key feature of the alignment is a 3.05km sea-crossing bridge, which will include navigational spans to allow maritime traffic to pass through to the ports of Prai and Butterworth.
The extension will provide a direct rail link between Penang island and Seberang Prai, connecting to Penang Sentral's multimodal transport hub for transfers to KTM services, ferries and buses.
Upon completion, the journey between Komtar and Penang Sentral is expected to take about eight minutes.
MRT Corp chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Zarif Hashim said the contract award brought Penang closer to establishing a seamless rail connection between the island and mainland.
"This extension reflects the vision of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who recognised that an investment of this magnitude must benefit communities on both sides of the strait," he said in a statement.
Zarif said the prime minister's goal was to ensure the project drives more inclusive economic development and opens up fresh opportunities for the public.
"With CMC2 now awarded, we are taking an important step towards fulfilling that aspiration.
"Our responsibility is to deliver not just the infrastructure, but the lasting benefits it promises," Zarif added.
MRT Corp said construction of the Mutiara Line LRT had reached 16 per cent completion and remained on schedule.
It added that comprehensive traffic management plans were being implemented in collaboration with relevant authorities to minimise disruptions to commuters during construction.
In August, MRT Corp awarded the RM3.03 billion system turnkey contract for the Mutiara Line LRT to a joint venture between Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) and Theta Edge Bhd.
The award
enabled railway systems
design and integration works to proceed alongside ongoing civil construction, marking another milestone in the development of Penang's first metro rail system.

Title: Dollar holds, yen gains as equity rout saps risk appetite ahead of payrolls
Article:
SHANGHAI/SINGAPORE: The dollar held steady against major currencies on Friday, after a sharp selloff in US equities drove investors toward haven assets such as the yen and pushed Treasury yields lower ahead of a closely watched government payrolls report.
The trigger for the retreat from risk was a Democratic sweep in Congress that hammered US stocks on Thursday, with the Nasdaq recording its deepest one-day drop since "Liberation Day" in April 2025.
Fears of tighter scrutiny of the artificial intelligence industry, particularly around data centre construction, has roiled global markets this week.
The equity rout prompted investors to find shelter in bonds and haven currencies. The yen strengthened 0.2 per cent to a one-week high of 157.40 a US dollar before reversing some of that gain.
The Swiss franc firmed 0.2 per cent against the US currency. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against six peers, was roughly flat at 101.55.
"The AI selloff is creating competing forces for the dollar," OCBC analysts said. "Falling US yields are blunting the dollar's safe-haven appeal, leaving the yen as the standout hedge against more US-centric volatility, while flows from Japan's Government Pension Investment Fund could provide another tailwind for the yen."
The flight to safety drove the 10-year Treasury yield down overnight. It was last trading at 4.84 per cent in the Asian morning, near its lowest level since Sept 10.
The two-year yield, which is more sensitive to interest rate expectations, fell about 10 basis points overnight to 4.47 per cent.
The move in bonds also reflected a repricing of Federal Reserve expectations, with fed funds futures scaling back the probability of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike in December to around 70 per cent from more than 80 per cent on Wednesday, traders said.
The euro was flat against the dollar at US$1.1222, but poised for a 0.5 per cent rise for the week, ending two weeks of loss.
Next on the agenda is Friday's US non-farm payrolls report from which investors will try and gauge the Federal Reserve's rate path. Data on Thursday offered an upbeat prelude, with weekly initial jobless claims falling by 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000 — matching a 57-year low in July and below the 196,000 estimate in a Reuters poll of economists.
"Recent data suggests improvement in the labour market, and we expect that to continue with this report," MUFG analysts said, referring to the non-farm payrolls data.
"Treasuries have just had a sizeable decline in rates heading into Friday's release. While we could see some of that move reverse, as long as we remain in a downward channel in rates, we recommend buying any meaningful dip on a stronger-than-expected number."
The sterling was last up 0.1 per cent at US$1.3457 after the Bank of England raised its policy interest rate as widely expected.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 200 families affected as flash floods hit Saujana Utama [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR: About 200 families in Taman Seri Alam,
Saujana Utama
, here, were affected by flash floods after a retention pond overflowed following prolonged rain yesterday afternoon.
Saujana Utama Residents Representative Council and community development chairman Wan Ismail Hashim said water from the pond spilled over into houses after it could no longer hold the volume.
He said the retention pond did not burst, unlike in previous incidents.
"Based on early estimates, about 200 families in Taman Seri Alam were affected by the overflowing retention pond.
"Water levels varied by area. Some reached knee height, but in most affected houses in Seri Alam, the water was estimated to be about 0.3m deep," he said when contacted.
Wan Ismail said Saujana Perdana also saw spillage, though floodwaters only reached car porches in the SU4 area as of yesterday afternoon.
Continuous heavy rain also caused a drainage bund to burst near the Eco Grandeur boundary, while several surrounding retention ponds reached maximum capacity.
"The retention pond could not cope with the volume, while outflow into the river slowed because river levels were already high.
"The Kuala Selangor Municipal Council deployed two water pumps, one each in Taman Seri Alam and Saujana Perdana.
"The pumps channelled water from monsoon drains and residential areas into the retention pond, but the impact was limited because the pond's own water level was already high," he said.
Wan Ismail said surrounding development and drainage maintenance issues contributed to the flooding, along with the prolonged rain and slow water outflow.
He said relevant authorities must pay attention to periodic maintenance of drains and drainage systems, particularly main outlets channelling water away from residential areas.
"Development played a part. Drain maintenance is also an issue, though it is not entirely due to development.
"Heavy rain and slow outflow are factors as well. I urge the relevant authorities to give extra attention to scheduled maintenance," he said.
Wan Ismail said joint monitoring by the council, police, district office, and residents' representatives was continuing to keep the situation under control.
He said the situation was improving following intervention by relevant agencies working together with residents.
"The rain has stopped for now. Our concern is that if it rains again, the water will rise.
"So far, water levels have receded slightly, but some areas still have stagnant water that has yet to drain off," he said.
He added that the district administration was prepared to open a temporary relief centre at Dewan Ixora Hillpark if conditions worsen and evacuations become necessary.

Title: Motorcyclist killed, another seriously hurt in trailer accident in Sungai Petani
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: One motorcyclist was killed and another seriously injured after their motorcycles brushed against the side of a trailer while they were trying to shelter from rain on the North-South Expressway.
The incident happened around midnight at Km96.2. Mohd Khairul A'zami Mohd Nazeri, 23, from Kampung Permatang Kong, Mukim Padang Hang, Alor Setar, died at the scene.
The other motorcyclist, also 23 and from the same village, is being treated at Sultan Abdul Halim Hospital.
Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said both victims were travelling from Alor Setar towards Sungai Petani in the left lane.
"When they reached the location, they tried to stop beneath the flyover to shelter from the rain.
"As they tried to avoid another motorcycle that had stopped there, their two Yamaha Y15ZR motorcycles brushed against each other before hitting the side of a trailer in the same lane.
"Both motorcyclists fell beneath the middle section of the trailer and were run over and dragged along," he said in a statement today.
Hanyan said the trailer driver was uninjured and the deceased's body was taken to the HSAH Forensic Department for a post-mortem.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
"The 40-year-old driver from Bayan Lepas, Penang, was taken to the Kuala Muda district police Narcotics Crime Investigation Division for screening and tested negative for drugs," he said.

Title: Trump takes action to make sure the Oval Office stays oval
Article:
WASHINGTON: Even as he puts his golden imprint on the White House, President Donald Trump moved on Thursday to protect two of its most historic spaces, the Oval Office and Cabinet Room, from major modifications by future presidents.
Trump signed a proclamation that he said would be the first step towards declaring the West Wing spaces a national monument to mark their place in American history.
It was unclear what exactly led Trump to seek protection of the structures from Congress now. There has been no move to tear down or dramatically alter the spaces.
The proclamation notes that the White House is already recognised as a national historic landmark but "nonetheless, the Oval Office merits specific recognition and protective management as a discrete historic structure of national significance". Trump said his proclamation would need congressional approval.
"So if they want to say 'let's not have Oval anymore, let's make it square,' what happens is they have to go back to Congress, and hopefully the Congress... will be smart enough not to let that happen," Trump said.
The action came two days after midterm elections that cost Republicans control of Congress. Democrats will assume the majority in January, curtailing Trump's legislative influence in the final years of his presidency.
Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has transformed the Oval Office with gold accents, paved over the Rose Garden, torn down the East Wing to make way for a ballroom, resurfaced the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and more.
The changes have faced opposition and, in some cases, court challenges, but nothing thus far has dissuaded the president.
[[nid:1571900]]
Environmental groups criticised Trump after he signed orders in July slashing the size of two national monuments in southern Utah by more than 90 per cent to allow for grazing, motorised recreation, logging and other resource development in the region.
Trump's signing ceremony on Thursday marked the third time this week he had promoted his pet projects. On Monday, in what was billed as his closing argument to voters ahead of Tuesday's elections, he unveiled his refurbished Reflecting Pool.
On Wednesday, the day after Republicans' election rout, he gave reporters a tour of the ballroom construction.
Trump cited the history of the Oval Office and Cabinet Room as the reason for needing to protect them. Both locations are the sites of major international and domestic meetings and have been in the same locations since the 1930s.
In a nod to the looming change in control of Congress, a red hat bearing the word VETO sat on Trump's desk during the signing of the proclamation.
As reporters were led to the Cabinet Room for a quick tour, Trump was asked if the next president would be allowed to take down all his gold decorations.
"They can do anything they want," Trump said, "as long as they do it carefully."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit opens lower amid mixed US economic and market signals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened lower against the US dollar on Friday, as mixed signals from the US economy and financial markets weighed on the greenback's outlook.
At 8am, the local note eased to 4.0450/0520 against the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0445/0490.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index edged up 0.03 per cent to 101.60, supported by signs of resilience in the US labour market.
He said the labour market indicator, such as initial jobless claims, fell further to 189,000 last week, suggesting the US labour market remained healthy.
"Still, the two- and 10-year US Treasury yields dropped 12 and five basis points to 4.46 per cent and 4.83 per cent, respectively.
"This suggests that the markets seem unconvinced about the rate-tightening cycle and perhaps also indicates that the scope for rate hikes has gradually diminished," he told Bernama.
Afzanizam added that the planned expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) data centres would come under further scrutiny by the US Congress in 2027, potentially affecting optimism over valuations in the sector.
This development could weigh on optimism about the sector's valuation. At the same time, the sharp decline in technology-related stocks suggested investors had become increasingly wary of the premium attached to the sector.
"On that note, the ringgit is likely to stay within a narrow band of RM4.04 to RM4.05 today," he said.
The ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.
It appreciated against the euro to 4.5413/5492 from 4.5428/5478 at Thursday's close, edged up vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.4421/4516 from 5.4455/4516, but fell versus the Japanese yen to 2.5683/5729 from 2.5548/5578 previously.
Meanwhile, the ringgit performed mixed against its Asean peers.
It gained versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1646/1706 from the previous close of 3.1679/1717, and increased against the Thai baht to 12.0836/1122 from 12.1013/1199 yesterday.
The local currency inched down versus the rupiah to 223.7/224.1 from 223.6/224.0 from Thursday's close, and was flat vis-a-vis the Philippine peso at 6.42/6.43.

Title: Japanese bonds rally as tech rout drives demand for safer assets

Title: Investors wipe US$2.5 trillion off Nasdaq as blue tsunami prompts AI fears
Article:
NEW YORK: Tech-led Nasdaq notched its deepest one-day drop since 'Liberation Day' in April 2025, wiping out trillions in market value on fears of more artificial intelligence (AI) scrutiny, particularly on data center construction, after Democrats won big in US midterm elections.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5 per cent on investor fears that the Democratic Party's sweeping midterm victory could stall AI infrastructure expansion and force a reckoning for smaller firms whose capacity to raise funds has already been limited by higher interest rates and tighter financial conditions.
It was the second straight day of selling in AI stocks and the fifth decline of more than 500 points in the Nasdaq Composite since mid-October, as the previously buoyant AI trade has come under increasing scrutiny in the last several weeks.
"The big election outcome was, especially with the Democrats winning a lot of the governorships, that the slowdown of the data center buildout is the real key theme that's going to stick," said Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading in Stamford, Connecticut.
The Nasdaq Composite is now in correction territory, having lost nearly 12 per cent from its record close on October 6. A correction is defined as a 10 per cent drop from a recent peak.
Many analysts said the scale of the declines suggests further selling is at hand, likely starting with Friday's market sessions in Asia. Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi have risen more than 20 per cent this year, but they fell significantly following Wednesday's rout in data center shares.
Some analysts wondered if the scale of the wipeout could affect the timing of Anthropic's blockbuster initial public offering expected this fall, as any delay could amplify market sentiment.
Analysts and portfolio managers said declines in once-hot areas such as semiconductors and AI infrastructure weren't entirely surprising, given the scale of earlier gains in many stocks and the financing concerns that have shadowed neocloud firms such as Nebius and CoreWeave since US interest rates climbed late in the summer.
Chip and neocloud shares posted the most significant declines on Thursday, reflecting worries that data center buildouts worth billions of dollars could face delays. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index fell 12 per cent to touch its lowest level in more than six months. Nvidia dropped nine per cent and Advanced Micro slumped 17 per cent.
Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX index of expected price swings, posted its largest increase since December 2024.
LOSING BIG IN A ONCE-HOT SECTOR
Hyperscalers, which defied Wednesday's AI selloff, also dropped. Amazon.com and Alphabet each slid 2.2 per cent. The Nasdaq 100 index, composed of the biggest names in the broader index, fell 6.4 per cent, erasing US$2.5 trillion in market value.
The selling suggests investors are starting to factor in increased local opposition to the data center buildout, with some analysts saying markets have yet to fully consider the costs it has imposed on US communities.
"There's going to be a lot of pushback about those data centers being geographically located in someone's backyard, straining the power grid, straining the water systems," said Bruce Zaro, managing director at Granite Wealth Management in Plymouth, Massachusetts. "Although there are a number of data centers already approved, there are still a lot to be permitted. There's going to be a difficult road to get those permitted forthcoming."
Around 30 per cent of expected US data center capacity additions in 2028 could be at risk from potential construction pauses, UBS analysts estimated, threatening an industry whose growth depends on a rapid buildout of new facilities.
The political jitters are hitting an AI trade already on shaky footing due to worries about the return on investment for the enormous sums being poured into the technology.
AI WINNERS WILT
Neocloud company CoreWeave, which has become a barometer of investor anxiety over heavy AI spending and borrowing, slumped 10 per cent. Its five-year credit default swap spreads , which measure market expectations of a potential default, widened to a record 1,267.9 basis points (bps), according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data.
Spreads on Intel's five-year credit default swaps also hit a record 149.7 bps.
Nebius, another neocloud company, dropped 15 per cent. Shares of both firms have dropped by half or more since the Nasdaq Composite hit a record on Oct 6.
"The market's moving from the promise of AI to the price of AI," said Ted Parkhill, founder and chief executive officer of Incline Investment Management.
"There's no question that AI is going to be transformative for the world in the long run. But that doesn't mean every AI-related stock is currently priced appropriately. There's going to be a lot of turmoil."
Data center operators Applied Digital, Cipher Digital and IREN tumbled more than 14 per cent each.
The weakness extended to utilities and equipment suppliers exposed to the buildout. GE Vernova fell 7.4 per cent, while Constellation Energy slipped 2.5 per cent.
Microsoft declined 3.6 per cent. The company is tightening oversight of some data center projects from Nebius, IREN and Nscale, Bloomberg News reported.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Silicon Valley faces Democratic reckoning after betting on Trump
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: Silicon Valley bosses who spent two years cosy­ing up to US President Donald Trump now face a Democratic Congress already threatening subpoenas, after midterm elections in which antipathy towards artificial intelligence swayed voters.
"AI company CEOs should be called to testify under oath," Greg Casar, chairman of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, said on Tuesday.
Senator Ed Markey, for his part, warned tech executives they would need to "plant new forests for all of the subpoenas we'll be printing".
It is a cold shower for tech bosses who rallied behind Trump after his 2024 win, with Elon Musk, Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and others front and centre at his January 2025 inauguration.
Musk went furthest, spending more than US$250 million to help elect Trump and then taking charge of his DOGE cost-cutting drive. He poured nearly half a billion dollars more into backing Republicans in the midterms.
Once they take control of both chambers on Jan 3, Democrats will control the committees that can compel executives to testify or hand over internal documents under threat of prosecution.
In 2020, the heads of Amazon, Apple, Facebook and Google were called to answer for their market dominance.
Musk, OpenAI's Sam Altman or Nvidia's Jensen Huang — one of Trump's closest advisers on AI — could now face the same ordeal.
Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, elected senator for Michigan despite more than US$5 million being spent against him by America PAC, the political committee funded by Musk, wants to go further.
He is calling for a "full-on pause" in the development of the most powerful AI systems and a US-China treaty to "pause and ban superintelligence", meaning AI that would surpass human intelligence.
To pass legislation, however, lawmakers will need to rally a party divided on the issue and overcome Trump's veto. He remains president until January 2029.
No major tech boss had commented on the election as of Thursday except Musk, who joked: "Data centres in space looking pretty appealing right now."
Parts of the industry had begun distancing themselves from Republicans before the vote.
The main pro-AI political fund, financed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz — one of whose co-founders backed Trump in 2024 — received no new donations from April through the end of September, as public distrust of AI grew.
Meta has hired former Democratic staffers in recent months to represent it in Congress, according to Axios.
'Shapeshifters'
Criticism is also coming from the Republican side.
"Voters are primed to reward whichever political party delivers on holding Big Tech accountable," Daniel Cochrane, a senior fellow at the conservative Institute for Family Studies, told AFP.
"In this election, concerns about AI's social and economic impacts shifted votes," he said, pointing to data centres as well as AI's effects on jobs and children.
According to an NBC News exit poll, AI and data centres were "a crucial or a major factor" for 56 per cent of voters in their choice for Congress.
"Let's not confuse an anti-Trump wave with an anti-tech mandate," said Adam Kovacevich, CEO of Chamber of Progress, an influential centrist coalition funded by major tech companies.
"There's only one thing that sinks the US economy, it's the AI trade," and "the only way to sink the AI trade is to sink the data centres," Chamath Palihapitiya warned during an election-night livestream of the All-In podcast, which he co-hosts with other prominent pro-Trump Silicon Valley investors.
Even market analyst Dan Ives, known for his bullish outlook on tech growth, now estimates that 10 per cent of the 800 to 1,000 new data centres planned in the United States "will not happen".
"The tech bros are shapeshifters," said Cochrane, who expects Zuckerberg "to have another mea culpa" before an "aggressive Dem Congress".
"Ultimately, the tech bros are for the tech bros," he said.
