Title: ‘You all know better’: Rosmah says no knowledge of RM50m fine payment to secure Najib’s house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has denied knowing anything about arrangements to settle the RM50 million fine that would allow her husband, former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
According to a report by the
New Straits Times
, she told reporters at the Kuala Lumpur courts complex that the family had been kept in the dark about any payment developments today.
“I do not know. You all know better,” she said.
“The family does not know and I am not being told about it.”
Her comments came after she attended a hearing for her application to introduce fresh evidence in her solar hybrid corruption case.
Reporters then showed her a Malay daily report claiming two individuals, said to be Najib’s representatives, were seen at the court’s payment counter this morning.
A puzzled Rosmah asked who the two were.
“They always know better and then after that they retract,” she said, referring to the Malay dailies.
Utusan Malaysia
had earlier reported that the two individuals were believed to have sought information on the procedures for paying the fine.
She also distanced herself from Umno’s crowdfunding drive to raise the RM50 million, saying she was not involved and directing questions to party secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
Asyraf Wajdi on Wednesday denied Najib was preparing to pay, noting the crowdfunding campaign had yet to hit its target.
He declined to reveal how much the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund, launched on September 18, had collected.
Lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah has also said he received no instructions from Najib to settle the fine.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar confirmed on Sunday that the fine remains unpaid and that no deadline has been set.
Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon on September 18, permitting him to serve the rest of his term under house arrest until August 23, 2028, provided the fine and other conditions are met.
Najib, 73, has been at Kajang Prison since August 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million from SRC International Sdn Bhd.
His original sentence was 12 years’ jail and a RM210 million fine, which the Federal Territories Pardons Board reduced in January 2024 to six years and RM50 million.

Title: EC sets Sarawak state election for Dec 12, nomination Nov 28
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 6 — The Election Commission (EC) has set the polling date for the 13th Sarawak Election on Dec 12.
EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the nomination date has been fixed on Nov 28, while early voting is on Dec 8, allowing a campaign period of 14 days.
Ramlan said this at a press conference after chairing EC’s special meeting to discuss the matter here today. — Bernama

Title: Speaker tells ministers to be on time after Health Ministry no-show in Dewan Rakyat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Members of the administration have been urged to arrive early for Dewan Rakyat sittings instead of waiting for their turn to speak, ensuring smooth proceedings and avoiding absences that reflect poorly on the House.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the admonition followed an incident during this morning’s sitting when questions could not be answered due to the absence of the relevant parties.
He said such situations arise when Members of Parliament (MPs) scheduled to ask questions cannot attend for unavoidable reasons, resulting in their questions being skipped.
“Naturally, the Speaker will skip the question, as happened this morning. The Minister or Deputy Minister is outside, unaware because, according to the order paper, their turn is still far off. When their turn comes, they are not present either, so the Speaker has to skip it as well. As such, this does not portray a good picture.
“I would like to advise members of the administration to arrive early and be in the Dewan even if your question number is scheduled later,” he said before the winding-up session of the debate on the Supply (Budget) 2027 Bill and the 2027 Development Expenditure Motion at the committee stage for the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW) in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
Johari also requested ministry officials, particularly secretaries-general, to advise ministerial officers to regularly check for changes in the question sequence with the Dewan Rakyat secretariat.
“This is because at the last minute, names or question numbers sometimes change due to requests from ministers or other unavoidable reasons that we have to accommodate,” he said.
He said all parties must play their role in improving the conduct of Dewan Rakyat sittings, especially now that the institution has administrative autonomy.
Earlier, several opposition lawmakers raised concerns over the absence of Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad and his deputy, Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib, from answering questions during the Question Time session in the Dewan Rakyat this morning.
Their absence was noticed after Deputy Speaker Alice Lau called on Zahir Hassan (PH-Wangsa Maju) to ask the third question addressed to the Ministry of Health, as listed in the Order Paper.
During the session, the second question scheduled for the Ministry of Transport was skipped after the MP for Kepala Batas, who was supposed to table the question, was absent from the lower house of Parliament, causing the session to move on to the next question.
However, the minister or deputy minister responsible for answering the next question was outside the hall, so that question was also skipped when their name was called. — Bernama

Title: JPJ issues over 133,000 summonses to foreign drivers in eight months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — A total of 133,081 summonses were issued to foreign drivers between January and August this year for various traffic offences, including driving without a valid licence.
In a written reply published on the Parliament website, the Transport Ministry (MOT) said the action was taken under subsection 26 (1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333), which provides for a fine of between RM500 and RM2,000, or imprisonment for up to three months, or both, upon conviction.
The ministry said the Road Transport Department (JPJ) recorded 21,232 offences for not having a Competent Driving Licence (CDL), while offences for not having a Goods Driving Licence (GDL) and a Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licence totalled 1,933 and 85 cases, respectively.
“Other offences recorded included expired Motor Vehicle Licences (LKM), lack of insurance, absence of an entry permit or International Circulation Permit (ICP), as well as overloading.
“The ministry also emphasised the responsibility of vehicle owners and employers to ensure that only individuals with valid driving licences are allowed to drive on the road,” it said in reply to a question from Dr Siti Mastura Muhammad (PN-Kepala Batas) on cases involving foreigners driving motor vehicles without valid driving licences.
It also said foreign nationals, including holders of United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards, found driving without valid licences would not be offered the option to pay a compound fine, but would instead be charged in court.
“Seizure action under Section 64(1) of Act 333 is also taken against foreign nationals involved in traffic offences. JPJ statistics showed that 3,572 vehicles were seized in 2025, while 7,445 vehicles were seized from January to October 2026.
“The same provision also prohibits any party from employing or allowing a person without a valid driving licence to drive. Action can also be taken against vehicle owners or employers who allow foreigners to drive without the requisite qualifications and valid documents,” the ministry said. — Bernama

Title: Overseas scammers targeting Malaysians can now face action, says Bukit Aman CCID
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have welcomed the government’s move to strengthen the country’s legal framework through the Cybercrime Bill 2026, particularly provisions allowing legal action against offenders operating from overseas.
Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said such action could be taken if the offences involved computer systems in Malaysia or Malaysian victims.
He said cybercrime and online scams were no longer confined by geographical boundaries, with syndicates operating from overseas using digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI) technology and identity impersonation to target victims in Malaysia.
“The cross-border jurisdiction provisions provide a clearer legal basis for investigations and enforcement action against offenders operating overseas,” he said in a statement today.
Rusdi said stronger investigative powers relating to data preservation and disclosure, traffic data collection and the interception of communications were also important in tackling cybercrime.
He said the provisions would strengthen PDRM’s efforts to combat online scam syndicates, improve investigative effectiveness and deter criminals who believed they could evade the law by operating across national borders or through digital technology.
“The CCID remains committed to ensuring that cyberspace does not become a safe haven for criminals.
“Combating cybercrime requires relevant legislation, responsive enforcement capabilities and cooperation between agencies and countries to protect the public from increasingly complex digital threats,” he said.
Today, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said in a written parliamentary reply published on the Parliament’s official website that Clause 2 of the Cybercrime Bill 2026 allows legal action to be taken against offenders overseas as if the offences had been committed in Malaysia.
He said implementation of the Bill would strengthen enforcement agencies through more responsive investigative powers and cross-border jurisdiction provisions to curb cybercrime, including online scams involving AI.
The Cybercrime Bill 2026, passed by Parliament last July, was drafted to repeal the Computer Crimes Act 1997 (Act 563) and address gaps in the law, including those relating to cross-border cybercrime and the misuse of AI technology. —  Bernama

Title: Govt reviewing e-hailing platforms’ 20pc commission cap, says Transport Ministry as 170,944 drivers opt into new fee
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The government is reviewing the commission cap for e-hailing platforms following calls by drivers to reduce the current 20 per cent rate, with the Ministry of Transport stating that the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) will study the cap in depth.
In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, the ministry said the review would follow engagement sessions with stakeholders and ongoing studies.
The reply was issued in response to Tebrau MP Jimmy Puah Wee Tse, who asked the Transport Ministry about the government’s efforts to discuss and urge e-hailing platform Grab to lower its 20 per cent commission rate for e-hailing drivers to ensure greater fairness and increase their income.
The ministry noted that Grab has proposed a new fare structure under a Proof of Concept (POC) known as the Grab Service Fee (GSF).
This structure uses flexible commission rates for daily trips but maintains a 20 per cent cap for the weekly or monthly average, taking into account distance, location, travel time and the real-time movement from a passenger’s drop-off point to a new pick-up location.
As of May 31, 2026, about 170,944 driver-partners had opted into the new structure.
The ministry recorded an average GSF of 18 per cent and an effective GSF of 15 per cent under the POC.
“The transit-per-minute income of driver-partners who joined the new structure recorded a continuous increase of over 6 per cent since the POC began,” it stated.
Grab updates the status and development of the POC to the Ministry and APAD regularly.
However, the government acknowledged drivers’ concerns about lowering the commission rate to increase their income more transparently and fairly.
The final review will also consider the outcome of ongoing studies by the Transport Ministry and the Human Resources Ministry regarding gig worker compensation, which are expected to be completed this year.
Note: The Land Public Transport Agency is known as Agensi Pengangkutan Awam Darat (APAD) in Malay.

Title: Transport Ministry: Govt keeps RM499 fare cap for Sabah and Sarawak routes, expands FLYsiswa for students
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The government will continue its intervention measures to keep flight fares between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah and Sarawak affordable amid rising operational costs, including maintaining a RM499 fare cap and expanding the FLYsiswa student subsidy initiative.
In a parliamentary reply yesterday, the Transport Ministry said aviation fuel accounts for 30 to 40 per cent of airline operating costs.
The reply was issued in response to Jerantut Member of Parliament Khairil Nizam Khirudin, who asked about the government’s intervention mechanisms to ensure that flights between Sabah, Sarawak and the Peninsula remain affordable amid the West Asia conflict and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.
“When fuel prices spike during a crisis, the government and its agencies have implemented several intervention measures,” the reply stated.
One key measure was the RM50 flight ticket rebate for travel between May 15 and June 14, 2026.
The rebate benefited 100,000 Malaysian passengers, with a total subsidy allocation of RM5 million.
The government also extended the credit period for Route Air Navigation Services charges from 30 to 60 days.
Similarly, airport operator MAHB extended the credit period for non-Passenger Service Charge elements to 60 days to ease airlines’ financial pressure.
The government has also postponed the implementation of new charges for Passenger Boarding Bridges and Check-in Counters for two months, and agreed to exempt aircraft parking charges for Malaysian airlines when appropriate.
To ease the burden on students, the ministry will continue the FLYsiswa initiative, which provides ticket subsidies for domestic routes between the Peninsula, Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan.
The initiative covers students at public universities, polytechnics, community colleges, matriculation colleges and teacher training institutes, and has been expanded this year to include students at Aswara, ILJTM, government-linked universities, state-owned higher education institutions and IMPAC.
For the festive season, the ministry also maintained a maximum one-way fare cap of RM499 (excluding taxes and fees) for travel from the Peninsula to Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan, down from the previous RM599 cap.
The subsidy period has also been extended from three to four days before major festive dates for 2026, covering Chinese New Year, Hari Raya Aidilfitri, Kaamatan, Gawai and Christmas.

Title: DAP focused on defending four Melaka seats, says Anthony Loke
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 6 — DAP is focusing on retaining the four seats it currently holds in the 16th Melaka state election, its secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said.
He listed the seats as Kota Laksamana, Bandar Hilir, Kesidang and Ayer Keroh and added that the party would also seek to capture three other seats - Duyong, Gadek and Pengkalan Batu.
“We are aware that there will be strong challenges in Duyong, Gadek and Pengkalan Batu. Nevertheless, we will work hard to win these seats,” he told reporters after attending the Malam Harapan programme at Pay Fong High School Hall in Jalan Tan Chay Yan here last night.
The programme was attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, and Parti Amanah Negara president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
Asked about the cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in facing the Melaka state election, Loke said it was a challenge that PH would have to contend with.
“When they (BN and PN) do not contest against each other and ask their respective supporters to support their cndidates, this gives them an advantage and presents a challenge for us.
“Nevertheless, we will continue to strive because, in any election, we must do our best to gain the support of the people,” he said.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka State Election, while early voting will take place on Nov 10. — Bernama

Title: Govt relaxes raw rare earth export moratorium to attract investors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The government has agreed to provide flexibility regarding the existing moratorium on the export of raw rare earth element (REE) materials through the Guidelines for the Conditional Export of Raw Rare Earth Elements in order to attract potential investors.
The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) said that currently, potential REE investors appear reluctant to invest due to the lack of a guaranteed, stable domestic supply of raw REE materials.
According to the ministry, this export flexibility is limited strictly to research and development (R&D) activities.
“Furthermore, the relevant company must demonstrate a clear commitment to collaborating on the development of processing facilities in Malaysia within three years from the date the export of raw REE materials is approved,” said MITI in reply to a question from Shaharizukirnain Abd Kadir (PN-Setiu) regarding the government’s firm stance on a US$96 million rare earth oxide supply agreement between Lynas and the Pentagon of the United States.
MITI said the ministry’s strategy focuses on attracting domestic and international investments to develop and subsequently strengthen the midstream and downstream segments of the REE industry, particularly in high-tech manufacturing areas such as permanent magnets, advanced materials, electronic components and batteries.
To realise the aspiration of developing a national REE industry, Malaysia must leverage strategic partnerships and technology transfers both domestically and from partner nations with expertise in REE processing.
“This initiative will not only bolster local capabilities across the entire value chain, from mining activities to the manufacturing of end-products, but will also position Malaysia as a key player in the global supply chain for critical minerals,” it added. — Bernama

Title: ‘This is the beauty of Malaysia’: Anwar’s Deepavali message calls for harmony
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on all Malaysians to use the Deepavali celebration as an opportunity to continue fostering goodness, mutual respect, and harmony within a multicultural and multi-faith society.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar said that despite cultural and religious diversity, the people share the same values - love, understanding, and the desire to live together in peace and harmony.
“This is the beauty of Malaysia that we must continue to preserve. Happy Deepavali to everyone celebrating!” he said.
Anwar also uploaded a two-minute-12-second video highlighting his visit to the 2026 Deepavali Mega Bazaar in Brickfields, here, yesterday.
Hindus across the country will celebrate Deepavali, also known as the Festival of Lights, this Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Man arrested for threatening Cheras trader with knife in viral video
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 – A 38-year-old man was arrested for allegedly making threats using a knife against a trader on Jalan Tasik Selatan 21, Bandar Tasik Selatan, Cheras, this afternoon.
Cheras District Police Chief ACP Rosdi Daud said the arrest followed an incident where a man was believed to have been slapped and threatened with a knife during a disagreement over roadside business activities in front of Residensi Sateri at 3:00 pm today.
He said that the local man was detained at a nearby banana fritter stall to assist with the investigation, and police also seized the knife used in the incident.
“Preliminary checks revealed that the suspect has no prior criminal record, and the case is being investigated under Section 323 and Section 506 of the Penal Code,” he said in a statement today.
He added that the investigation paper is currently being finalised, which includes recording statements from the victim and witnesses, as well as securing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage around the scene of the incident.
Earlier, a video depicting the incident went viral on social media. — Bernama

Title: Seven arrested as external syndicate behind pilot drug smuggling, no KLIA insiders involved
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Police are investigating whether there was internal involvement at KLIA after a Malaysian pilot was arrested in Jakarta for allegedly smuggling 26 kilogrammes of drugs.
The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) confirmed the arrest of the pilot in Jakarta on July 29, 2026, according to a written parliamentary reply yesterday.
The reply was issued in response to Kepong Member of Parliament Lim Lip Eng, who asked the Home Ministry for the status of the investigation into the case and whether there was any involvement of internal parties at KLIA.
“The subject is currently undergoing investigation by the Indonesian authorities to be charged under Indonesian laws on drug smuggling and trafficking,” the reply stated.
Following the arrest, PDRM obtained further information from Indonesian authorities between August 11 and 15, 2026.
This intelligence helped police identify the syndicate network, including those who supplied, sent, and managed the syndicate’s finances.
Between August 20 and September 6, 2026, police crippled the syndicate and arrested seven Malaysian citizens.
Regarding the alleged involvement of KLIA insiders, police conducted investigations into aviation security, including the AVSEC Division.
“Based on the investigation results, there are no indications showing the involvement of any flight crew or internal parties at KLIA in the drug smuggling activity,” the reply stated.
Investigations found that KLIA procedures and security measures were implemented according to established standards.
The government stated the activity was organised by an external syndicate without indications of involvement from airport officers or ground crew.

Title: Melaka polls: Anwar urges voters to pick reps with ‘direct line’ to PM’s office
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 6 — Voters in the Melaka State Election are urged to choose elected representatives who have a ‘direct line’ to the Prime Minister’s Office to ensure smooth development processes and the protection of local residents’ welfare.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) Chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said good relations and alignment of direction between the Federal administration and state assemblymen at the State Legislative Assembly level are vital to ensuring the smooth implementation of development projects and public welfare policies.
Citing the PH candidates for the Paya Rumput and Kelebang state seats as examples, Anwar said both candidates share the same direction as the Federal Government, and their credibility and integrity are greatly needed to effectively translate government policies at the grassroots level.
“I look after the country, and I want those who represent us to help follow this line - they must follow this policy. So can our representative here, Tok Man (Datuk Azman Abidin) in the Paya Rumput DUN, help? Let there be a direct voice to my office. Similarly with our young female candidate (Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir) in Kelebang - pleasing in appearance, good at work, and hardworking,” he said.
Anwar, who is also the Prime Minister, said this when delivering his speech at the Ceramah Perdana Melaka Rumah Kita for the Paya Rumput state assembly seat here tonight.
According to him, having elected representatives who possess a ‘direct line’ and close working relationship with the nation’s top leadership provides a major advantage to voters in bringing any infrastructure, drainage, or socioeconomic issues directly to the government’s attention.
Therefore, Anwar reminded voters in the Melaka state election to make wise assessments when choosing leadership by electing candidates who truly work for the people, rather than those who merely stoke sentiments throughout the campaign.
Meanwhile, speaking at a separate event while attending the MADANI Sinar Deepavali Celebration at the Kampung Permai Main Hall in Machap Umboo here, Anwar said he is optimistic that PH can secure a victory in the 16th Melaka state election on Nov 14.
“I know they say, ‘Oh, Melaka is not a PH stronghold.’ I know it’s not a PH stronghold... Selangor was never a PH stronghold before either, nor was Perak.
“Yes, (politics) has its ebbs and flows, but this time I believe we can start bringing change - we start bringing change here in Melaka to save the country,” he said.
The Election Commission has fixed Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka PRN, with early voting on November 10. — Bernama

Title: Da’i Syed rape acquittal: AGC to seek Court of Appeal review
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) will file a review application against the Court of Appeal’s majority decision yesterday acquitting independent preacher Da’i Syed, or Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohammad Shaiful, of a rape charge.
“The Attorney General’s Chambers takes note of and respects the decision made by the Court of Appeal on Nov 5, 2026 through a majority decision acquitting and discharging Syed Shah Iqmal of the charge under Section 376 of the Penal Code,” the AGC said in a statement yesterday.
“After reviewing the grounds of judgment by the Court of Appeal panel, the Public Prosecutor has decided that a review application will be filed under Rule 105 of the Rules of the Court of Appeal 1994,” the statement read.
The AGC said the application would be based on legal principles and the criteria and threshold set for the exercise of the Court of Appeal’s review jurisdiction, as outlined in the Federal Court’s decision in Asean Security Paper Mills Sdn Bhd v Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance (Malaysia) Bhd.
“Accordingly, the prosecution’s submissions will focus on the question of whether there are exceptional circumstances that meet the legal threshold, enabling the court to consider the exercise of its review jurisdiction,” the statement read.
The AGC said it took note of and respected the Court of Appeal’s decision and remained committed to upholding the rule of law and ensuring that justice is served through the legal channels and provisions in force.
Yesterday, Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid, in a 2-1 majority decision, acquitted and discharged Syed Shah Iqmal of the charge of raping a woman in 2019, while Justice Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid upheld the conviction and sentence.
The panel reached the decision after allowing Syed Shah Iqmal’s final appeal against the conviction and the 10-year prison sentence and three strokes of the cane imposed by the Shah Alam Sessions Court.
On Dec 10, 2020, Syed Shah Iqmal pleaded not guilty to a charge of raping a then 23-year-old woman at a condominium in Shah Alam around 1.35 am on Sept 11, 2019.
He was charged under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum of 20 years’ imprisonment and caning upon conviction.
On April 10, 2023, the Shah Alam Sessions Court acquitted and discharged him after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against him at the close of the prosecution’s case.
The Shah Alam High Court, however, ordered him to enter his defence on the charge after allowing the prosecution’s appeal.
On Jan 23 this year, the Shah Alam High Court dismissed his appeal and upheld the Sessions Court’s decision, prompting the celebrity preacher to take the case to the Court of Appeal, while the prosecution filed a cross-appeal against the sentence. — Bernama

Title: KLIA to get AI body scanners, K9 relocation under new 17-point security plan to curb drug smuggling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The government has approved a phased security enhancement plan for Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) that includes 17 substantive recommendations to curb drug smuggling.
The Cabinet approved a joint memorandum from the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry on August 19, according to the official parliamentary reply published yesterday.
The reply was issued in response to Kota Melaka MP Khoo Poay Tiong, who asked the Home Ministry about steps to strengthen security protocols at KLIA following a six-fold surge in drug seizures at the airport to RM108.35 million in the first seven months of 2026.
The action plan is based on three core security pillars: aviation security, national and border security, and physical security and protection.
“Phase 1 of the short-term recommendations focuses on optimising the closing of control gaps using existing powers, personnel, and assets,” the reply stated.
This first phase includes tightening the e-Vetting screening for security passes, enforcing random drug tests on pilots and flight crew, and increasing the omnipresence of police personnel.
It also covers the proposed relocation of the police K9 Narcotics Unit and the Customs Department at special departure zones and risky baggage areas.
The medium-term phase, running from six to 24 months, focuses on building new capacities and procuring high-tech strategic assets.
These include the supply of high-powered baggage scanners and body scanners, as well as the installation of CCTV with artificial intelligence analytical capabilities.
The long-term phase, exceeding 24 months, is committed to modernising national security systems comprehensively.
This includes replacing baggage and body scanners with new-generation AI technology across all entry points, and modifying terminal and cargo infrastructure based on risk levels.
It also involves establishing the National Immigration Command Centre (NICC) as the national intelligence hub, and expanding uniform, integrated security control standards across all air, land and sea entry points in the country.
The government acknowledged that Malaysia’s strategic geographic position and extensive transport network have made it a potential transit route for international drug syndicates.

Title: Sarawak’s 13th state election dates to be announced today as EC meets
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 6 — Sarawak’s election calendar takes shape today as the Election Commission (EC) convenes a special meeting to lock in the key dates and arrangements for the 13th State Election.
The meeting, chaired by EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun at a hotel here, will be followed by a press conference.
The press conference is expected to announce the election writ date, nomination day, polling day, the electoral roll to be used and other election matters.
On Oct 23, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced that the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly had been dissolved effective Oct 26, paving the way for the 13th Sarawak State Election.
Under Article 21(4) of the Sarawak State Constitution, the election must be held within 60 days of the date of dissolution.
The current mandate of the 82-seat Sarawak State Legislative Assembly is due to end in February 2027.
In the 12th state election held on Dec 18, 2021, Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS), led by Abang Johari, secured a strong mandate after sweeping 76 of the 82 seats contested, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) won four seats and the DAP secured two.
The state’s political landscape, however, saw a shift following PSB’s dissolution in 2024, when three former assemblymen from the party joined the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP), one of GPS’s component parties.
Meanwhile, another former PSB assemblyman, See Chee How, who represented Batu Lintang, left the party and became an independent assemblyman.
GPS comprises Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), the Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP. — Bernama

Title: Motorcyclist sheltering from rain under Sungai Petani flyover dies after being run over by trailer, another seriously hurt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — A motorcyclist was killed and another seriously injured when a trailer struck them as they sheltered from rain under a flyover at Kilometre 96.2 of the North-South Expressway near Sungai Petani early this morning.
Kuala Muda district police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the two men, both 23 and from the same village, had stopped under the flyover to escape the rain, according to a
Berita Harian
report.
“When trying to avoid another motorcycle that had stopped to take shelter under the flyover, both Yamaha Y15ZR machines brushed against each other before scraping the side of the trailer in the same lane,” he said in a statement.
The trailer then ran over and dragged both riders, killing Mohd Khairul A’zami Mohd Nazeri of Kampung Permatang Kong, Mukim Padang Hang, Alor Setar, at the scene.
His companion is receiving treatment at Sultan Abdul Halim Hospital.
The two were travelling in the left lane from Alor Setar towards Sungai Petani when they stopped at the location.
The 40-year-old trailer driver from Bayan Lepas, Penang, was not injured and tested negative for drugs in an initial screening.
The body was taken to the hospital’s forensic department for a post-mortem.
Police are investigating the case under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: Free AI, tax breaks and business grants in Budget 2027 — how Malaysians stand to benefit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Malaysians who pay for ChatGPT or other AI apps will be able to claim the cost as tax relief under Budget 2027, one of several measures proposed to get more people and businesses using artificial intelligence (AI).
The budget also adds 100,000 free AI subscriptions for young people and sets aside RM30 million to help small businesses adopt the technology, alongside longer-term spending on skills, research and a sovereign AI cloud, as part of the government’s goal of making Malaysia an AI nation by 2030.
Who gets the additional 100,000 free AI subscriptions?
The existing AI Untuk Rakyat programme offers 100,000 Malaysians aged 18 to 30 three months’ free access to selected AI apps once they pass six learning modules on the Rakyat Digital portal.
Current providers are YTL AI Labs, Alibaba and Google.
Budget 2027 adds another 100,000 places and brings in more apps, including ChatGPT.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the expansion followed a strong response to the first round.
What support is available for businesses adopting AI?
The government has allocated RM30 million through the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) to help 4,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) adopt AI and automate their operations.
MDEC is a government agency responsible for driving Malaysia’s digital economy.
Its work includes helping businesses adopt digital technologies, supporting digital start-ups and attracting investments into the country’s digital sector.
For smaller businesses, adopting AI can involve more than subscribing to a chatbot, while financial support could help businesses that lack the resources to implement these systems independently.
The programme will also train and certify 5,000 AI professionals, helping to develop the workforce needed to support wider adoption.
However, the RM30 million allocation should not be interpreted as a fixed grant for every business.
The amount available to individual applicants, qualifying expenses and application requirements will depend on the programme’s implementation details.
Businesses interested in participating should look out for further announcements from MDEC.
Can you claim tax relief for ChatGPT and other AI subscriptions?
Yes, Budget 2027 proposes expanding individual lifestyle tax relief to include subscriptions to AI software and applications.
As specified under the Finance Ministry’s tax measures, the relief will cover subscriptions for personal use, as well as those purchased for a spouse or child.
This means taxpayers who pay for eligible AI services, including subscription-based applications, could claim the expenses when filing their income tax returns.
However, this is not a separate tax relief ceiling for AI subscriptions.
The proposed expansion means taxpayers will be able to include eligible AI subscription fees alongside other qualifying expenses, subject to the overall RM2,500 ceiling.
This expansion is proposed to take effect from the 2027 year of assessment, meaning it will apply to eligible expenses incurred in 2027 when taxpayers file their returns in 2028.
The measure is intended to encourage digital literacy and wider adoption of AI technology by making subscription costs more affordable.
Budget 2027 proposes expanding the existing RM2,500 individual lifestyle tax relief to cover eligible AI software and application subscriptions from the 2027 year of assessment. — AFP pic
How much is being spent on AI skills and research?
The government is allocating almost RM15 million to AI Malaysia Berhad to strengthen a safe and ethical AI ecosystem, with a target of developing 200,000 AI-skilled workers.
AI Malaysia Berhad is Malaysia’s national lead agency for AI, established under the Digital Ministry to coordinate the country’s AI development and implementation.
The initiative reflects the need to equip Malaysians with skills relevant to industries increasingly using AI.
These capabilities could include understanding how AI systems work, applying them to business operations and developing technology responsibly.
Separately, RM6 billion will be allocated across ministries for research, development and commercialisation of innovations.
This is a broader allocation rather than funding exclusively for AI, intended to support research and technological development that contribute to Malaysia’s wider innovation ecosystem.
Safeguards for data
Under Budget 2027, the government is planning a sovereign AI cloud to ensure the public’s data and the country’s strategic information remain under Malaysian control.
AI systems rely on computing infrastructure to process information, run applications and, in some cases, train models.
Cloud services allow organisations to access this computing capacity remotely rather than maintaining all the necessary equipment themselves.
A sovereign AI cloud aims to give Malaysia greater control over the infrastructure and data used in these operations.
This is particularly relevant when government agencies and businesses handle sensitive information, including personal records and confidential commercial data.
Protection will also depend on access controls, cybersecurity measures and rules governing how information can be used.
According to Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, the initiative would be managed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Communications Ministry.

Title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain in eight states and Labuan tonight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas in eight states and Labuan till 10pm tonight.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said that the affected areas include Kubang Pasu, Baling, Sik and Padang Terap in Kedah; Lipis, Raub, Cameron Highlands and Rompin in Pahang, along with Larut Matang, Kampar, Kinta, Kuala Kangsar, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Hulu Perak, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Batang Padang and Selama in Perak.
Other areas include Gua Musang in Kelantan, Hulu Selangor, Kuala Selangor, Gombak, Sabak Bernam and Klang in Selangor, as well as Kota Tinggi, Johor Bahru and Mersing in Johor.
Finally, in Sarawak, the affected areas are Miri (Marudi, Telang Usan, Bario and Beluru) and Limbang, while in Sabah, Pensiangan, Sipitang, Beaufort, Kuala Penyu and Tenom in the Interior are affected. — Bernama

Title: Election of first Muslim to US Senate is lesson against racial politics, says Anwar
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 5 — The historic election of the first Muslim to the United States Senate should serve as a lesson for all on the importance of rejecting racial prejudice and religious discrimination, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He cited Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s victory in Michigan as an example of how political participation could transcend racial and religious differences.
Anwar said the development reflected growing political acceptance of diversity and demonstrated that democracy should provide opportunities for people of all backgrounds, rather than be driven by racial sentiment.
“They understand democracy and reject racism. Those who defeated President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the United States are people who oppose racism.
“They campaigned against racism and religious oppression, bringing a new message. When racism gains ground, Muslims and other minorities are the ones who suffer,” he said at the Melaka Madani Aspirations Tour programme for Klebang constituency at Taman Bukit Rambai here today.
El-Sayed, a Democrat, won Michigan’s Senate seat in the US midterm elections, becoming the first Muslim elected to the Senate.
Anwar said the victory demonstrated how rejecting racial prejudice could become a powerful message for political change.
However, he stressed that Malaysia need not emulate the US political model, as the country had its own identity as a prosperous, multiracial nation. — Bernama

Title: Zahid urges ‘respect’ between BN, Perikatan as Melaka campaigning intensifies
Article:
ISTANBUL, Nov 5 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has reminded all party machinery to exercise restraint and conduct their campaigning responsibly during the 16th Melaka State Election.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said that while campaigning between BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) had intensified, there had also been several clashes that should have been avoided.
“My stand, as well as that of the chairman of the coalition on the other side (PN), is that we should respect what we have mutually agreed upon.
“Although there is no formal agreement, mutual understanding is very important,” he told Malaysian media after a pre-meeting with the country’s representatives and delegation in conjunction with his working visit to Turkiye here today.
Ahmad Zahid said excessive campaigning, including raising issues unrelated to the state election, would not change the stance or decisions already made by voters.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will take place on November 10.
For the latest news on the Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Flash floods hit Sungai Buloh, Puncak Alam after heavy rain (VIDEO)
Article:

Malay Mail
also sighted an overflowing flood retention pond at Taman Seri Alam in Saujana Utama, Sungai Buloh, with water gushing into a nearby residential area.
According to
Harian Metro
, other affected areas included Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Puncak Alam, Alam Suria and Jalan Meru near the Kampung Bukit Cerakah junction.

Title: Tengku Puteri Zainah, former wife of Najib, dies at 70
Article:
KUANTAN, Nov 5 — Tengku Puteri Zainah Tengku Eskandar, the mother of Pahang Investment, Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee chairman Datuk Mohamad Nizar Najib, died today. She was 70.
Mohamad Nizar, who is also the Peramu Jaya assemblyman, shared the sad news in a post on his Facebook page.
“It is with deep sorrow that I announce the passing of my beloved mother, Tengku Puteri Zainah,” the post read.
The eldest son of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak also expressed his appreciation for his mother’s love, sacrifices, and prayers.
“Nothing can ever repay all your deeds. May
Allah
forgive all your sins, grant His mercy, and place you among the dwellers of heaven.
“Mother, you’ll remain in my prayers and memories forever.
Al-Fatihah
,” he wrote.
Tengku Puteri Zainah had previously been reported to be in critical condition while receiving treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of a hospital in the capital. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar: No reason to keep CSA secret, Cabinet to discuss disclosure tomorrow
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 5 — The government has no objection to disclosing the contents of the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) signed between the Unity Government, Bersatu and independent Members of Parliament, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said there was no reason to keep the agreement confidential and that he would raise the matter with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, who oversees the arrangement, at tomorrow’s Cabinet meeting for further action.
“I have no objection to making it public. In fact, the draft and principles are similar to the agreement between Pakatan Harapan and the previous government comprising PAS, Bersatu and Umno.
“It was their party (PAS) that proposed such an agreement in the first place, together with Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin and several others in the government at the time.
“Yet they are now questioning it. It is rather strange when their own members have not read or thought about it,” he told reporters after officiating the Prime Minister’s Golden Hand Awards 2026 ceremony at Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) here today.
Anwar was responding to PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan’s call for the government to disclose the contents of the agreement.
Asked about PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s description of the CSA as a “devilish approach”, Anwar said the remark was inappropriate.
“Tan Sri Hadi is a religious scholar, and his statements should be more measured. He tried to explain that his remarks were not directed at me, and that is fine, but it is inappropriate to label a person, group, or position as devilish.
“How is it that when they do it, it is not devilish, but when others do the same, it becomes devilish? I do not think religion should be used in that manner,” he said.
On October 29, the Madani Government signed a CSA with six Bersatu MPs led by party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and seven others, including Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman. — Bernama

Title: Nilai teen tests positive for three drugs after dazed vaping video prompts police investigation
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 5 — A male secondary school student in Nilai has tested positive in a preliminary urine screening for three types of drugs, namely ketamine, benzodiazepines and THC.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the 17-year-old student was being investigated following the circulation of a video on social media showing him allegedly in a dazed state after vaping.
Alzafny said the video was believed to have been circulated on October 28 at a secondary school in the district.
“Police took note of the video circulating on the Threads platform on November 4 before launching an investigation and identifying the student involved.
“However, the preliminary urine screening results are still subject to further confirmation. In this regard, a police report has been lodged in connection with the incident,” he said in a statement here today.
Alzafny said the student would be referred to the National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) for further action under Section 3(1) of the Drug Dependants (Treatment and Rehabilitation) Act 1983. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak eyes 2050 plan to spread jobs, services and growth beyond major cities
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 5 — Sarawak is considering a long-term urban development policy through 2050 to guide settlement planning and ensure balanced development across major cities, smaller towns and rural areas.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the proposed Sarawak Urban Development Policy 2050 would provide long-term direction for the state's urban and settlement system, taking into account its vast geographical landscape and diverse communities.
He said the policy should be aligned with statutory plans, development decisions, infrastructure programmes and accountable delivery arrangements to ensure that strategic planning translates into effective implementation.
“Through the Post COVID-19 Development Strategy 2030, we seek to advance economic prosperity, social inclusivity and environmental sustainability as mutually reinforcing objectives,” he said.
He said this during his closing keynote address titled “Leadership for Better Cities: Our Shared Responsibility”, at the 11th National Planning Congress 2026, Dewan Sivik Majlis Bandaraya Petaling Jaya, here today.
Elaborating further, Abang Johari said Sarawak recognised the importance of developing a strong settlement system that connected urban centres with their surrounding regions.
“Kuching, Sibu, Bintulu, Miri and our growing towns should play complementary roles in providing services, employment and economic opportunity,” he added.
Abang Johari said development planning should also take into account the different needs of smaller towns, riverine settlements, rural communities and interior areas.
He noted the state should not expect every settlement to become a metropolitan centre, but instead ensure that each had access to appropriate services, connectivity and economic opportunities.
He emphasised that strategic plans must guide land use, transport, housing, public facilities and environmental protection in a coordinated manner, with clear outcomes, responsible agencies and the necessary resources for implementation.
“We do not claim to have solved every challenge...but we believe consistent policy direction, institutional cooperation and a commitment to measurable outcomes provide the foundation for progress,” he said.
Abang Johari said the true measure of development was whether it delivered tangible benefits to the people, such as shorter journeys to work, better homes, more reliable public services, safer neighbourhoods and lower household expenses. — Bernama

Title: RM1.5m facelift for Penang Assembly includes heritage gallery, lactation room and upgraded media area
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 5 — The Penang State Legislative Assembly has implemented several infrastructure improvements and upgrading works at its building here, involving a cost of RM1.5 million.
This was undertaken in conjunction with the Second Meeting of the Fourth Session of the 15th Penang State Legislative Assembly.
Its Speaker, Datuk Seri Law Choo Kiang, said the works involved improvements to both the interior and exterior of the building, including a comprehensive structural inspection through a dilapidation report and roof maintenance.
He said among the new facilities provided was a dedicated lactation room for breastfeeding mothers, in addition to improvements to the staff rest area to provide a more comfortable environment with greater privacy.
“In addition, the State Assembly Building Gallery has been rebranded as ‘Warisan Visual Terukir’ (Engraved Visual Heritage) to showcase the history and contributions of Penang State Assemblymen who have served from 1959 to 2026,” he said in a statement today.
He said the upgrading efforts also included the provision of a Special Officers’ Room equipped with workspaces, printing facilities and audio-visual equipment, as well as improvements to the State Assembly Meeting Room, which can now accommodate up to 25 people at any one time.
Law said the special media conference area had also been upgraded to provide greater comfort for media practitioners covering the assembly sitting.
The upgrading works will continue after the sitting concludes, including improvements to the disabled-friendly toilet near the guardhouse and the renovation of the general storeroom to ensure that equipment used during assembly sittings can be stored in a more orderly and organised manner. — Bernama

Title: Batu Caves ritual video: Youth repents publicly with family at Shah Alam mosque
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 5 — A 21-year-old Muslim youth whose participation in Hindu rituals at a Batu Caves temple sparked a controversy made a public declaration of repentance today alongside his mother and younger sister, prior to undergoing court-ordered faith rehabilitation.
Reciting the Islamic declaration of faith before state religious officials at the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Mosque here, Aliff Daniel Adli renounced the Hindu and Buddhist rituals he had previously engaged in, acknowledging that his actions violated Islamic tenets and caused widespread distress.
“I once again declare that, without coercion from any party and in good faith, by uttering the words, ‘There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah’, I repent to Allah with sincere and genuine repentance,” he said during the ceremony, vowing not to repeat the acts and committing to study Islamic doctrine under qualified religious guidance.
His mother, Rohizayanti Ramli, and younger sister, Nur Ranea Ezreen Adli, made their own formal declarations of repentance, expressing regret over failing to guide and counsel him away from external influences that conflicted with Islamic teachings.
An emotional Rohizayanti admitted that parental lapses and a lack of religious grounding had contributed to her son's misstep.
“I acknowledge all forms of negligence, carelessness and shortcomings in fulfilling my fundamental duties and responsibilities as a mother,” she said, pledging to attend religious classes and work closely with Islamic authorities to guide her son.
Nur Ranea similarly expressed remorse for not providing adequate advice to shield her brother from external influences, committing to support him through prayer, family care, and ongoing cooperation with religious bodies.
Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said the public ceremony was held to confirm that all three family members have genuinely repented and returned to the fold of Islam in accordance with Ahli Sunnah Wal Jamaah teachings, while easing community anger following the viral video clips.
“We want to demonstrate through this declaration that he has genuinely repented. Hopefully, Muslims who were initially angry or disappointed with Aliff Daniel will realise that we are all human and we make mistakes.
“We can now see for ourselves that Aliff Daniel has repented and wants to return to the teachings of Islam,” he said at a brief press conference later.
Salehuddin disclosed that the Syariah Court has ordered Aliff Daniel to undergo three months of mandatory faith rehabilitation at Pusat Pemurnian Akidah Baitul Iman in Hulu Yam, Selangor.
During his stay, he will receive structured Islamic instruction from accredited teachers, followed by long-term monitoring and pastoral guidance from the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS).
The MAIS chairman expressed hope that Aliff Daniel would eventually help encourage his mother and sister to attend regular classes at their neighbourhood mosque, while urging social media users who may have been influenced by his past posts to disavow any practices that run counter to Islamic teachings.

Title: Ramanan: Mitra allocates RM755,390 to upgrade facilities at 21 Tamil schools in Melaka
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 5 — The Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra) has allocated RM755,390 to 21 Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) in Melaka this year to enhance teaching and learning facilities.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the allocation covered various initiatives, including MADANI furniture assistance, tuition classes and digital learning tools such as smartboards.
“The programmes are implemented through collaboration between Mitra and the Education Ministry, as well as school administrators and boards of governors, to ensure students benefit from the assistance,” he said during a visit to SJKT Jasin Lalang in Ayer Merbau here today.
Ramanan said SJKT Jasin Lalang had received RM47,560 under the initiatives.
He said Mitra had also introduced various educational assistance programmes this year for Indian students at all levels, from preschool to public and private higher education institutions.
“Our approach covers the entire education ecosystem to ensure targeted groups receive assistance tailored to their needs at every stage of learning.
“These initiatives also focus on expanding access to technology and digitalisation in schools,” he added. — Bernama

Title: No transfer letter received, Shuhaily remains border agency chief, lawyer says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Embattled Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MBCA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has yet to receive an official transfer letter from the Home Ministry, leaving him legally empowered to lead the agency despite ministerial statements that he is being returned to the police force.
Counsel Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali confirmed that in the absence of a formal administrative directive, his client remains fully authorised to execute his duties at the helm of the national border agency,
FMT
reported.
“To date, he has not been found guilty of any offence. He can therefore continue to carry out his duties as usual,” he said when met at the court complex here.
Rafique called on Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail to address the administrative ambiguity, arguing that public pronouncements of an impending transfer had generated confusion and invited unnecessary speculation.
“People are now questioning why the minister has announced one thing while what is happening on the ground suggests otherwise. Saifuddin should clarify this matter as it has given rise to speculation,” he said.
The clarification follows Saifuddin's announcement last week that the Home Ministry had decided to terminate Shuhaily's secondment to MBCA and return him to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
However, despite being described as “on leave” the preceding week, Shuhaily returned to active duty on Monday, formally chairing an MBCA commanders' operational meeting.
Shuhaily, who formerly headed Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department, was seconded to lead MBCA on a two-year contract commencing July 1 last year.
His tenure was thrust into the spotlight after he claimed trial at the Sepang Magistrate's Court on Oct 21 to two counts of voluntarily causing hurt under Section 323 of the Penal Code, involving an alleged altercation with two Special Branch officers at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in late September.
Any premature termination of his posting also faces a constitutional hurdle.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail previously clarified that because Shuhaily's two-year tenure was granted with the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, any decision to truncate his contract requires the formal assent of the King before taking legal effect.
